reason: Verified in source and by driving. render-b.js binds `on:{click}` to exactly four elements in the whole direction — the .b-step date steppers. act(), bar()'s .b-switch, the per-row .b-grab, the .b-seg visibility pair and .b-undo's button are all `h("button",...)` with no handler and no delegated listener anywhere in render-core.js. Driven at 1440: in owner-flight all 11 buttons report NO CHANGE on click, Enter and Space on a focused .b-grab report NO CHANGE; in owner-editing the -7 stepper correctly moves invitations 23 -> 'in 16 days' but the .b-undo button and Ctrl+Z both leave it at 'in 16 days', Done leaves .b-edit count at 1, Escape leaves it at 1, and 'Take it off the plan' leaves .b-item count at 7; owner-empty's 'Set the day' reports NO CHANGE. The affordance claim is also exact: .b-item measures 520x79 with a 24px/600 title, its only button is the 54x28 'shown' badge, and elementFromPoint over the title returns .b-title — so the owner cannot reach owner-editing except by editing the URL. This is not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs asserts only that the stepper moves the edited item and that a reversibility surface exists, is role=status, carries a button and names a key — it never asserts that the button or the key does anything. And it is a named, paid-for defect class: lessons.md 'Keyboard models advertised but not implemented — advertising is a promise; the panel checks promises', plus 'Nothing reversible'. Fifteen focus-ringed, hover-styled (.b-act:hover, .b-grab:hover, shell.css :focus-visible) controls promise verbs that do not exist, and the aria-label on the badge says 'Open to change it' — the promise is spoken aloud to a screen reader. No constraint is touched: no colour, no weight, no family, no reopening of the locked direction.
